(edenvia/avatars/lymphatic-bloating.md). Every line points to a source ad (#n) or a tool. Nothing invented.

Lymphoria sells a different product (herbal "lymphatic drainage" drops) to the same buyer and the same desire: feel lighter,

less puffy, legs and belly that finally respond. We clone the buyer, the structures and the proof devices. We never clone

the product claims (herbs, "drain", disease names).

2. Five secondary angles

  1. Results timeline as the angle itself (24 hours / 1 week / 4 weeks, or week 0 / 4 / 8, or day 14 / 30 / 60): 20 of 35 statics carry one.

  3. Alcohol / beer as the trigger (#1, 14, 15): "after two weeks of regular drinking, alcohol paralyzes your lymphatic drainage."
  4. "The doctor told you to lose weight" (primary texts of #10, #11, A8 avatar language "dismissed by doctors"): the expert who let her down.

6. Avatar (what the ads show)

  • Who is on screen: two avatars, split by angle. Women 45–60 (menopause belly, wardrobe, jawline; #11, 19, 26, 29, 35) and men 45–60 (beer belly, dad bod, man boobs, tucked shirt; #1, 6, 14, 15, 17, 20, 30). Soft midlife bodies, ordinary clothes (tank top, T-shirt, button shirt), bathroom mirror, wardrobe, backyard. Never a fitness model, except as the week-8 "after" cartoon.
  • Visible problem: a belly that no diet moves, a jawline gone soft, swollen ankles and legs, back rolls, bat wings, foamy urine.
  • What they tried and spent: "no matter how hard you diet or workout" (#4/#9), eating less, the doctor's "lose weight" (A8 sheet), supplements graveyard.
  • Everyday shame behaviours (from the diary captions): shirt left untucked (#14), fitted clothes stay on the hangers (#19), folded inward when walking (#30), belly bloated by evening (#11).
  • Match with the founder's A8 sheet: exact. The sheet's avatar ("I had hated my legs my whole life… dieting harder, exercising more, never having results… it's not a fat problem") is Lymphoria's L4 + L3 buyer. The sheet skews female 35–55; Lymphoria spends more on the male belly (L1). Recommendation below keeps both.

9. Their offer

  • Price: $49.90 $18 per bottle (#17, 31, 34), "3 for $18 each" (#12), "5 for $17.99 each" (#25), Buy 2 Get 1 Free + up to 70% off (#16, 23, 27), "70% off tonight only" (#13).
  • Guarantee: 30-day money-back (#15, 16, 20, 26) but also 60-day (#18) and 90-day (#35): inconsistent across creatives.
  • Social proof: "90,000+ happy customers" (#15, 16, 20, 26), "200+ doctors recommend" (#35), "3rd party tested" (#16), "wild-harvested herbs".
  • Funnel: most spend goes to advertorial landing pages ("Harvard states 165 million Americans are living with a lymphatic dysfunction…"), product pages for the offer ads.

10. Their weaknesses (sourced)

  • Disease and condition naming in copy: PCOS (#11 text), menopause (#19, 26, 29), "lip edema" (their video), "liver failure" (Trendtrack #Dr. Micheal Jones ads). FTC/Meta exposure; Edenvia will not copy these words (brand.json bans them).
  • Inconsistent proof: 30 / 60 / 90-day guarantee; "90,000+ customers" vs "200+ doctors"; a "WEEK 4 · WEEK 4" typo on #20.
  • Creative sameness: one 2×2 timeline template cloned ten times; the audience sees the same layout for every body part.
  • Page churn: Brandsearch shows 0 active ads on the main lymphoria.co page and the spend moving through persona pages ("Ancient Roots" 4,542 ads / 227 k€ EU spend; "Herbalist Amara Linden, PhD"; "Lymphologist Allison James, PhD"); Trendtrack shows 10,382 statics across pages such as "Herbal Remedies" (~3,800 active), "Lymphatic Wellness Explained", "Dr. Micheal Jones". Fake-expert pages are a bannable pattern.
  • Scale: 5.4 M monthly visits (Brandsearch) and ~230 k€ measured EU spend on one page alone: Edenvia will not out-spend them; it has to out-specify (the molecule, the glass of water, 8 PPM) inside their proven structures.

11. Recommendation for Edenvia (A8) — the 3 angles and 10 headlines to attack first

Angles

  1. "It was never fat" — swollen legs and belly (L4 + L3, the founder's A8 sheet): the timeline on legs, ankles, belly; the mechanism in Edenvia's words (oxidative stress keeps the tissue inflamed and holding fluid; hydrogen, the smallest molecule, reaches it). King angle.
  2. Puffy face and jawline (L2): the most visible proof, the top active ad of the competitor. Same timeline device, face version.
  3. The man's belly that isn't fat (L1): the two biggest spends. Beer belly / dad bod / tucked shirt, with the then-vs-now and the mirror selfie as raw-photo advertorial openers.

10 headlines (rewritten for Edenvia: structure/function wording, no herbs, no "drain", no disease names; prices from brand.json)

  1. "Your swollen legs were never fat. It's fluid your body stopped clearing."
  2. "The heavy, puffy legs no diet has budged."
  3. "Her ankles, FINALLY BACK." (24 hours · 1 week · 4 weeks)
  4. "Your double chin's not just fat. It's years of fluid your cells stopped moving."
  5. "What a puffy belly actually is (it's not food)."
  6. "Goodbye heavy legs. Hello the old me."
  7. "Do not try this if you don't want these side effects: #1 waking up with a sharp jawline, #2 friends asking if you lost weight, #3 boots that zip again."
  8. "He wants his tucked shirt back." (diary timeline, man's belly)
  9. "You kept trying to shrink the fat while the thing keeping your legs swollen was still switched on."
  10. "One tablet. One glass of water. 8 PPM of hydrogen. Legs that finally feel light again. $39 (was $79.99), 30-day money-back."

These angles and headlines become the source for the step-2 specs. Lint will block any $ amount outside prices_allowed

and any disease, drug or competitor name.
